items.summary: Solid-state batteries use a solid electrolyte, replacing the more volatile liquid or gel electrolytes found in standard lithium-ion batteries, and are seen as one of the most promising battery technologies. By replacing traditional liquid electrolytes with solid materials, solid-state batteries offer increased safety as well improved energy density that is up to 50 per cent higher.

items.title: Solid-state batteries | MIT Technology Review
items.summary:
liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer, creating power packs that charge faster, last longer, cram more energy into smaller spaces, and (crucially) run cooler. A new generation of companies aim to bring such batteries to market, and if their bets pan out, the tech could substantially ease the shift away from fossil fuels. [...] Solid-state batteries have been “just a few years away” for more than a decade now. In laboratories, the technology works. But there have been challenges. In designs that pair the solid electrolyte with a lithium-metal anode (the side of the battery that releases electrons into an electrical circuit), needlelike filaments called dendrites tend to grow during charging, and they eventually push through the electrolyte and short the cell. Solid electrolytes are supposed to physically block the [...] # Solid-state batteries

Batteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.

items.title: Chemical Breakthrough Could Unlock the “Holy Grail” of Solid-State Battery Technology
items.summary:
Scientists in China have developed a thin protective coating that could help overcome a major obstacle to longer-lasting, high-capacity batteries. In laboratory tests, solid-state batteries using the treated lithium metal retained 82.3% of their initial capacity after 300 charging cycles, compared with just 43.0% for batteries using untreated lithium. [...] #### Stronger Performance in Laboratory Tests

The coated lithium electrodes withstood a critical current density of 3.5 milliamperes per square centimeter, more than four times the 0.8 achieved by untreated lithium. In complete batteries containing a nickel-cobalt-manganese oxide cathode and a sulfide solid electrolyte, the protected electrodes delivered an initial capacity of 129.8 milliampere-hours per gram and retained 82.3% after 300 cycles at 0.5C. [...] Solid-state batteries are a promising alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries because they replace flammable liquid electrolytes with solid materials. Credit: Stock

### A simple chemical treatment could overcome a persistent weakness in next-generation solid-state batteries.
